title: Simultaneous quotient realization of completed comparison diagrams
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ inside an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, their valuation rings and uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and composable scheme morphisms $Z\xrightarrow hX\xrightarrow fY$ with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $D=E,L$ and $W=Z,X,Y$, put $B^D_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_D/\varpi_D^n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site and $R_{D,W}=\lim_n B^D_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use whole normalized coefficient systems [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], coherent derived reduction $\mathcal R_D$, total limit $\mathcal L_D=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and the actual completed operations $\widehat F_f,\widehat T$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $M,N,H\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].

For every choice of flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q,J$ of $M,N,H$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $P_n=P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}B^E_{Y,n}$ and likewise for $Q,J$, with actual quotient transitions. Set
$$T_n=\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes Q_n),\quad U_n=f_n^*P_n,\quad V_n=f_n^*Q_n,\quad W_n=\operatorname{Tot}(U_n\otimes V_n).$$
Every finite well-typed expression in these towers, the coefficient units, total tensor and the pullbacks $f_n^*,h_n^*$ is a flat-term K-flat normalized system. Its canonical completed-operation substitution identifies its total derived limit with the same expression in the completed operations, naturally and compatibly with the coherent reduction counits. The comparisons $c_{f_n;P_n,Q_n}$, with formula $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ and inverse $(s\otimes x)\otimes(t\otimes y)\mapsto st\otimes(x\otimes y)$, form a strict tower isomorphism $c:f^*T_\bullet\cong W_\bullet$ [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence].

Under these substitution comparisons the maps $\mathcal L_E(c)$ and $\mathcal L_E(c^{-1})$ are the hom and inverse of the canonical completed comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison], and are natural in $M,N$ under all derived morphisms and independent of the simultaneous representatives. Writing $K_s=\widehat F_f\widehat T(M,N)$, $K_t=\widehat T(\widehat F_fM,\widehat F_fN)$, and $r_s:\mathcal R_EK_s\cong f^*T_\bullet$, $r_t:\mathcal R_EK_t\cong W_\bullet$ for the coherent counit comparisons, and $\beta_s:K_s\cong\mathcal L_E(f^*T_\bullet)$, $\beta_t:K_t\cong\mathcal L_E(W_\bullet)$ for the substitution maps, put $\gamma_E=\beta_t^{-1}\mathcal L_E(c)\beta_s$. One has the whole-system equation
$$r_t\,\mathcal R_E(\gamma_E)=c\,r_s.$$
The reassociation, signed symmetry, action-unit and pullback-composition diagrams formed on $P,Q,J$ with $c$ (and with the comparisons for $h$ and $f\circ h$) are commuting diagrams of these strict systems; their limit images are the corresponding commuting diagrams of $\gamma_E$ and the specified completed structural maps, including their coherent finite reductions.

Let $S_W$ be completed scalar extension from $E$ to $L$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. The scalar quotient representatives are
$$(P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}B^E_{Y,n})\otimes_{B^E_{Y,n}}B^L_{Y,n}\cong P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}B^L_{Y,n},\quad (x\otimes a)\otimes b\longmapsto x\otimes ab,$$
and similarly for $Q$. They and all the displayed tensor/pullback expressions are normalized systems with their actual transitions, including for ramified $L/E$. Write $\alpha_F:S_X\widehat F_{f,E}\cong\widehat F_{f,L}S_Y$ and $\alpha_{T,W}:S_W\widehat T_E\cong\widehat T_L(S_W,S_W)$ for the canonical scalar comparisons [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. If $\gamma_D$ denotes the completed comparison just specified for $D=E,L$, then
$$\gamma_L\,\widehat F_{f,L}(\alpha_{T,Y})\,\alpha_{F;\widehat T_E(M,N)}=(\alpha_{F;M}\widehat\otimes^L\alpha_{F;N})\,\alpha_{T,X}\,S_X(\gamma_E).$$
This is the limit image of the strict scalar-association square, whose two chain routes send $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. The square and its inverse retain all quotient transitions and obey identity and successive coefficient-extension equations. No flatness of $B^E_{W,n}\to B^L_{W,n}$ is assumed.

source.place: Integral level: compatible finite reductions and derived inverse limit; representative-normalized tensor, pullback and scalar diagrams elaborating the returned proof steps 4-10 of lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso (agent argument).

proof.text: Apply the quotient normalization theorem to obtain the actual normalized quotient expressions, invertible recursive substitutions, presentations and input naturality. Apply canonical identification to obtain the forward comparison equality and strict coherence/naturality at both coefficient fields. Apply scalar limit realization for the generated scalar closure and the two limit-image equations.

For a strict arrow v define c=beta_A L(Q(v)) beta_B^{-1}. Cancelling beta_B proves c beta_B = beta_A L(Q(v)). Apply reduction, then naturality of the actual adjunction counit: R(L(Q(v))) epsilon_B = epsilon_A Q(v). Reassociate to obtain R(c) r_B = r_A Q(v). This is the claimed whole-system equation.

The transport of a strict isomorphism is the composite of the source substitution iso, the limit of its derived iso and the inverse target substitution. The forward comparison equality therefore identifies its inverse with the canonical inverse by cancellation. For each structural isomorphism use the same conjugate; the preceding two equations prove both required squares. Any other candidate agrees after composition with the invertible target substitution, proving uniqueness.

Use the existing scalar tower unit, composition and quotientModels theorems verbatim for the remaining scalar identity, successive extension and balanced association clauses. Assemble all the clauses with the witnesses from quotient normalization.

Step 2: the exact functor R lim on the derived category of strict towers, applied to the strict isomorphism c and its inverse; generic homological tool of sk-thm-properbasechange, also declared by lem-pur-integral-coherence-tower and lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence.

Step 3: localization of flat-term K-flat complexes is D(R), and transformations of bifunctors extend uniquely from that subcategory; generic site tensor tool of sk-thm-properbasechange used as a black box, as in lem-pur-normalized-scalar-comparison-realization and lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model.
